column1: # Book 2 second-round read (Fable, 2026-10-30): every line read against the Latin. Opus gloss findings adjudicated:
# 2.472 unde est ... acerbum: the rough beginnings are the source of the bitterness, not what the sea consists of.
# 2.484-485 non possunt rendered once (it was doubled across the two lines).
# 2.539 tanta ferarum vis = so great a multitude of beasts (vis of number, as at 544), with Bailey.

column2: beginnings, from which the body of Neptune gets its bitterness,
body, for the shapes to vary much from one another
